Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-29

Attendees: Marco (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Leah (Redwood CSM), Tom (Opal ML), Rina (Opal Infra), Sam (Opal CISO), Jules (Product)

Auto-summary (auto generated, may be partial):
- Opal evaluating cost/unit tradeoffs across hosted, dedicated, and private (VPC) for a chat-based reconciliation assistant.
- Key constraints: 500M tokens/mo projection, 75-150ms token latency SLO for interactive flows, compliance (SOC2 + data residency EU), budget target $40k–$60k/mo initial.

Topics: cost per token, batching and KV cache opportunities, hosted vs dedicated capacity path, pilot timeline, encryption/KMS + audit log needs

Transcript body:
[00:00] Marco (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, um this is Marco from Redwood, i'm joined by priya on the eng side and leah from CSM, how's everybody doing?
[00:06] Tom (Opal): good thanks, Tom here, loud and clear.
[00:09] Rina: hi hi, rina here.
[00:11] Sam: sam, ciso, quick availability check, we're good.
[00:14] Marco: perfect, i'll keep this pretty focused — goal is to understand your token burn projections, latency targets, and any security constraints so we can point you to hosted vs dedicated vs private and a realistic cost per unit.

[00:27] Priya (Redwood SE): quick note — when we say token unit economics, we usually give per-1k-token generation and embed cost, and then we model the effect of batching and prefix/K V cache reuse which often moves the needle a lot.

[00:40] Jules (Product): our use case is customer reconciliation chat — multi-turn, lots of reminders and context, so we see long-ish histories per session. we projected 500M tokens per month after q2.
[00:52] Marco: ok that's helpful, 500M is in the range where dedicated capacity often becomes compelling because of predictable throughput and lower per-token marginal cost with reserved GPUs, but there are tradeoffs.

[01:05] Tom: can you quantify that trade? like, how much cheaper vs hosted for our numbers?
[01:09] Marco: sure i'll give a ballpark — with hosted you'd see a little higher per-token list price but no infra ops; dedicated can be 20-45% lower on per-token depending on batching and model quantization. but the real saving is when you can exploit KV cache across sessions and batching; that can drop effective tokens by 15-30% depending on re-use.

[01:30] Rina: we have EU data residency constraints and need to run in our VPC or a cloud region restricted to EU. does Redwood Hosted offer region isolation with audit logs?
[01:38] Marco: yes, hosted supports region selection for many regions — we can do EU regions, and you get audit logs and data controls; however, if you need complete network isolation and customer-managed KMS/HSM, that's where Redwood Private or Dedicated in a VPC comes in.

[01:55] Sam (CISO): quick one — can you describe the KMS/HSM flow? we need customer-managed keys and signed audit trails that are exportable.
[02:03] Priya: for Private we integrate with your KMS — we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and bring-your-own HSM patterns. audit logs are exportable to your SIEM and we include cryptographic attestations in the enterprise package. i'll send the integration docs.

[02:19] Marco: also note hosted can be acceptable if you accept provider-managed keys but still want SOC2 controls and tenant-level audit logs — many customers choose hosted first and migrate to private later.

[02:32] Tom: from a perf perspective, we need interactive latency — roughly 75 to 150ms per token on average for user flows, with occasional bursts for bulk reruns. is that feasible on hosted?
[02:42] Priya: short answer yes for many models, but it depends on model size, sequence length, and the hardware routing. our hosted standard tier targets Xms p50 and Yms p95 — (note: actual numbers redacted in call) — for sub-100ms p50 we'd usually recommend picking a smaller model variant or using a deduped prompt design and aggressive caching.

[03:04] Tom: ok, you mentioned batching — doesn't batching increase latency?
[03:07] Priya: it can if you wait to form batches, but we employ continuous batching where requests are batched on-the-fly so tail latency is minimally affected. plus you can set latency SLO policies per route: strict low-latency routes bypass batching or use smaller batch windows, lower priority bulk routes use larger windows and better cost.

[03:28] Rina: what's the expected headroom for autoscaling? we sometimes have traffic spikes from reconciliation runs at month-end.
[03:35] Marco: Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and configurable burst capacity; hosted can burst but is subject to region capacity and multi-tenant prioritization. if month-end spikes are critical you may want dedicated with burst buffers or a hybrid routing policy that falls back to a cheaper model variant when hot.

[03:52] Sam: security question again — are logs HIPAA-ready or does that need private?
[03:56] Marco: HIPAA is supported under our enterprise compliance package typically via Redwood Private or dedicated with specific DPA addendums. hosted can be configured for many compliance needs but we usually recommend private for the strictest requirements.

[04:12] Tom: you mentioned quantization — how big a difference does that make?
[04:15] Priya: quantization reduces GPU memory and often improves throughput. for many transformer models, moving from fp16 to int8 or 4-bit quantization drops per-token cost by 8-25% depending on quality tolerance. we provide quality regressions and eval tools to validate.

[04:33] Jules: sample economics — if we assume 500M tokens/month, average prompt+resp ~80 tokens, that's about 6.25M requests. what would be the monthly spend range?
[04:44] Marco: rough quick model: hosted with moderate batching might be in the $55k–$85k/mo range; dedicated with committed capacity and quantization could bring that into $35k–$60k/mo. these are rough — we'll run specific sims and share.

[04:59] Tom: are there hidden costs — networking, storage for KV caches, or per-route charges?
[05:04] Priya: good call — storage for prefix/K V cache is typically minimal but accounted for; we include network egress in the cost model where applicable; dedicated has operational/management fees and potentially support tiers. we'll itemize in the matrix.

[05:18] Rina: timeline — we want to pilot in June, production by Q3. is that realistic?
[05:24] Marco: yes pilot in June works; typical pilot is 4–6 weeks with a small dedicated pool or hosted configured with caching and key routes. we'll propose a 3-month pilot pricing to accelerate evaluation.

[05:36] Sam: what's the rollback / fallback story if a model fails or cost spikes?
[05:40] Priya: we offer smart routing and automatic fallback policies — route to cheaper model variants, route across regions, or fail closed with a cached response. you can configure thresholds for cost and latency to trigger fallbacks.

[05:55] Tom: can we run a benchmark with our prompt set? we want real numbers for p50/p95 and effective tokens after cache reuse.
[05:59] Marco: absolutely — Priya will run a perf sim and we can do a benchmark with your sample prompt set. please upload prompts to the shared spreadsheet or S3 link and we'll schedule the run.

[06:12] Priya: small caveat — for private/on-prem benchmarks we need a bit more lead time to provision dedicated infra or coordinate with your infra team for on-prem network. for hosted quick sims we can usually run within 48–72 hours.

[06:27] Rina: cost governance — we need per-route cost breakdowns and token-level attribution for chargebacks to product teams. do you expose that?
[06:33] Marco: yes the console provides token-level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and can tie tokens to API keys for internal chargeback. plus we have alerting for spend thresholds.

[06:45] Jules: what's the biggest gotcha customers miss when choosing hosted vs dedicated?
[06:49] Priya: many teams underestimate the impact of re-use patterns — if you have high cache hit rates, dedicated pays off faster. conversely, if you have very spiky, unpredictable workloads with lots of cold context, hosted's operational simplicity can be better. also model drift and evals — make sure you have continuous quality monitoring.

[07:10] Marco: ok let's recap and commit next steps. we'll send a cost matrix for hosted vs dedicated vs private with line items (model cost, reserved infra, support, storage, egress) and a pilot pricing option. Priya will run the perf sim and provide the effective token numbers with batching/k v reuse assumptions. Sam will share the compliance contact and audit window.

[07:30] Sam: i'll get that to you, likely early next week.
[07:34] Tom: we also want a kernel-level deep dive for the SEs, to understand how the KV cache is indexed and reused across sessions — can we schedule that?
[07:41] Priya: yes we'll do a kernel deep dive, probably 60min, demo the cache hit scenarios and kernel selection heuristics. i'll coordinate with Tom.

[07:53] Marco: perfect. any other questions?
[07:55] Rina: not for now. thanks.
[07:58] Jules: good meeting, thanks everyone.
[08:00] Marco: thanks all, we'll follow up with the matrix and docs. bye.
